question: What is the official name of JavaScript?
solution:
The correct answer is __**ECMAScript**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The official name of JavaScript is **ECMAScript**.
 
• ECMAScript is a standardized scripting language specification, created to ensure the interoperability of web pages across different web browsers.
 
• JavaScript was originally developed by Netscape as Mocha, later renamed to LiveScript, and then to JavaScript. However, due to trademark issues, the standardized version was named ECMAScript.
 
• ECMAScript is maintained by the ECMA International standards organization in the ECMA-262 and ISO/IEC 16262 specifications.
 
• There are several editions of ECMAScript, with ECMAScript 6 (ES6) being one of the most significant updates, introducing many new features and improvements to the language.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **ECMA International** is an industry association founded in 1961 dedicated to the standardization of information and communication systems.
 
• The first edition of ECMAScript was released in June 1997.
 
• Subsequent versions of ECMAScript have introduced significant features such as classes, modules, and async programming capabilities.
 
• JavaScript engines in web browsers, such as V8 in Google Chrome and SpiderMonkey in Mozilla Firefox, are implementations of the ECMAScript standard.
 
• ES6, also known as ECMAScript 2015, was a major update that included features like arrow functions, template literals, and destructuring assignments.
